claim.claim-text: 1. A first Ethernet switch (24) configurable for providing a first Layer-2 communication path between the first Ethernet switch and a second Ethernet switch (28) via a third Ethernet switch (36A) connected between the first and second Ethernet switches, a second Layer-2 communication path, that is different from the first communication path, between the first Ethernet switch and the second Ethernet switch (28) via a fourth Ethernet switch (36B) connected between the first and second Ethernet switches, and a third Layer-2 communication path, that is different from the first and from the second communication paths, between the first Ethernet switch and the second Ethernet switch (28) via a fifth Ethernet switch (36C) connected between the first and second Ethernet switches, the first Ethernet switch comprising:

a first port for receiving different first, second, and third groups of Ethernet frames; a second port connectable to the third Ethernet switch; a third port connectable to the fourth Ethernet switch; and a fourth port connectable to the fifth Ethernet switch, wherein the first Ethernet switch is configurable to transmit the first group of Ethernet frames only via the second port to the third Ethernet switch as part of the first Layer-2 communication path, wherein the first Ethernet switch is configurable to transmit the second group of Ethernet frames only via the third port to the fourth Ethernet switch as part of the second Layer-2 communication path, wherein the first Ethernet switch is configurable to transmit the third group of Ethernet frames only via the fourth port to the fifth Ethernet switch as part of the third Layer-2 communication path, and wherein the Ethernet frames are assigned to be carried over one of the first, second, and third communication paths based on respective results of a hashing function applied to their respective header value in a header field.

2. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 1, wherein the first, second, and third communication paths are associated with respective different first, second, and third index values (50), and wherein Ethernet frames associated with a hashing function result that is equal to the first index value are carried over the first communication path, Ethernet frames associated with a hashing function result that is equal to the second index value are carried over the second communication path, and Ethernet frames associated with a hashing function result that is equal to the third index value are carried over the second communication path.

3. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 2, wherein the third Ethernet switch comprises a fifth port (40A) that is part of the first communication path, wherein the fourth Ethernet switch comprises a sixth port (40B) that is part of the second communication path, wherein the fifth Ethernet switch comprises a seventh port that is part of the third communication path, and wherein the first, second, and third index values are respectively associated with the fifth, sixth, and seventh ports.

4. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 3, for use with a group of N distinct index values that comprises the first, second, and third index values, and wherein the hashing function results in a value from the group.

5. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 4, for use with a natural number N (N>2 or N=2), wherein the hashing function is based on modulo-N calculation, or wherein the hashing function is based on Exclusive OR, XOR, operation.

6. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 3, wherein the fifth port of the third switch, the sixth port of the fourth switch, and the seventh port of the fifth switch, are assigned to serve as member ports of a Multi Homing Group, MHG (44), and wherein all the frames transmitted from the first switch and destined to the second switch are received at one of the third, fourth, and fifth switches, or wherein the fifth, sixth, and seventh ports are each Media Access Control, MAC, addressed, and wherein the frames are further routed according to a MAC learning process or based on flooding.

7. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 1, wherein the first Ethernet switch comprises a Network Processor, NP, (46) for processing frames and a host processor (48) coupled to control the NP and to provide management and configuration.

8. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 1, further configurable so that the first, second, and third communication paths between the first and second Ethernet switches are configured for protection against failures or for providing traffic load balancing, or wherein the first Ethernet switch is configurable to provide a protection scheme that comprises using the first communication path for frames carried over the second communication path upon a failure in the second communication path.

9. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 8, wherein the protection scheme is according to, using, or is based on, International Telecommunication Union - Telecommunication Standardization Sector, ITU-T, G.8031 June 2006 standard, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, IEEE, 802.1D-2004 standard, IEEE 802.1 standard, or IEEE 802.1Q standard, or IEEE 802.3 Clause 43 standard.

10. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 8, further configurable for monitoring an activity status of the first, second, or third communication paths, and responsive to a change detected in the activity status or to a detected failure in one of the communication paths, sending a failure message.

11. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 10, wherein the failure message comprises a Wait-To-Restore, WTR, parameter, or is according to, or based on, International Telecommunication Union - Telecommunication Standardization Sector, ITU-T, G.8031 (June 2006) standard.
12. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 1, wherein the header field comprises an origin address or a Media Access Control, MAC, address.

13. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 1 for use with MAC-in-MAC encapsulation that is according to, based on, or compatible with, IEEE 802.1AH/D3.01 draft standard, wherein the header field comprises outer MAC address, service ID, I-SID, value, or any combination thereof, or wherein the first Ethernet switch is further configurable to provide Virtual Private Local Area Network Services, VPLS, and the frames comprises the VPLS identification in the header field or value.

14. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 1, wherein at least part of the frames are associated with, or are part of, a Virtual LAN, VLAN, and wherein the header field comprises a unique Virtual Circuit, VC, label, or wherein the header field comprises a VLAN Identifier, VID, that is according to, based on, or compatible with, IEEE 802.1Q standard.

15. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 14, wherein the at least part of the frames are associated with, or are part of, multiple VLANs deployed in a hierarchical structure, which include an outer VLAN, identified with an outer VLAN Identifier, VID, encapsulating an inner VLAN identified with an inner VLAN Identifier, VID, and wherein the header field comprises the outer VLAN Identifier, VID, or the inner VLAN Identifier, VID, that are each according to, based on, or compatible with, IEEE 802.1Q standard.

16. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 1, further configurable as edge node according to, compliant with, or based on, Spanning-Tree Protocol, STP, standard, Multiple Spanning-Tree Protocol, MSTP, standard, Resilient Packet Ring IEEE 802.17 standard, or Rapid Spanning-Tree Protocol, RSTP, that is according to, or compliant with, IEEE 802.1D standard.

17. The first Ethernet switch according to claim 1, for use in a network that comprises, or is part of, a ring topology network, or wherein at least part of the frames are broadcast or multicast frames or Address Resolution Protocol, ARP, frames.
